The review step is concrete, but the shipped script adds a `history.length > 1` condition. The spec decision names only a same-origin referrer and discusses `history.length > 1` as the rejected approach. The behaviour departs from the decision.

routes.json lists the route; tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers a query route, whitespace and #; test/traffic.test.js checks the listed routes including the query; the 'AC-11' test in index.test.js checks that every listed route answers 2xx.
The existing tests remain and the <li> assertion was updated. The code paths for healthz, 404, 405 and the escaping of titles are unchanged.
test/apply-migrations.js drops tables in one batch with deferred foreign keys. Test 'AC-13' leaves a categorised row and expects a clean count in the next test.

findings.what: The Go back script goes back only if `ours && history.length > 1`. The spec decision says it goes back when document.referrer is same-origin, and it names `history.length > 1` as the rejected approach. The extra guard is not in the decision. The AC-8 test regex does not check for it.
findings.fix: Remove `&& history.length > 1` so the condition is only the same-origin referrer, or record an owner decision in the spec for the extra guard.

findings.what: The state table has gaps in its tests. Row 2 (`/` with no items) only asserts 'No items yet.', not that the filter links are shown with All current. Rows 1-4 never assert that the 'Go back' link is hidden on 200 pages.
findings.fix: In the empty-table test, assert the nav and the All current link. In the 200-page tests, assert that 'Go back' and the script are absent.

findings.what: The 404 page uses the title and h1 'Broken link'. The spec only specifies the message and the Go back link.
findings.fix: Keep only the specified content, or leave the extra heading and title as they are, since the spec does not forbid them.
